text: According to McTaggart, what is distinctive about the B-series relations earlier-than, simultaneous-with, and later-than?
choices: They are permanent and tenseless: if E1 is earlier than E2, that holds timelessly and never changes
They continually change, as what is future becomes present and then past
They require an objectively moving present in order to order events
They hold only in the present moment and cease to exist as time passes
explanation: B-series relations are permanent and tenseless: that the Battle of Hastings is earlier than the French Revolution holds timelessly and never alters. Option 1 describes the A-series, whose properties change as the present moves; option 2 imports the moving-spotlight A-theory; option 3 states presentism. Only option 0 captures the fixed, tenseless character McTaggart assigned to the B-series.
